newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICAN BANK LAUNCHES WESTERN CAPE PROPERTY FUND.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICAN BANK LAUNCHES WESTERN CAPE PROPERTY FUND.

text.p: South Africa's Cape of Good Hope Bank and Property Asset Managers on Thursday launched a regionally focused property fund aimed at institutional investors.
Property Asset Managers managing director Royden du Plooy told a media briefing that the Western Cape Property Fund would be open-ended and unlisted with a target portfolio of 200 million rand.
Old Mutual has already invested 10 million rand in the fund and Du Plooy said that because it would be carefully geared and flexible, it could outperform cash or listed property funds.
Du Plooy said that the fund could continually add to its portfolio and its value would not be affected by fluctuations on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange.
"Research shows that the Western Cape is well positioned to benefit from the up trend in the long term property cycle," Du Plooy said.
This was because regional growth was ahead of other provinces, the limited availability of land in the Peninsula and the lower crime rate in the province.
The fund's proposed portfolio weighting will be 50 percent industrial, 25 percent retail, 15 percent commercial and 10 percent leisure.
It has already bought three properties, including industrial and business parks, with initial yields of up to 12 percent.
